diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, pattern B
legend: Focal destructive invasion is seen at the front of an otherwise exophytic tumour with papillary architecture. Single glands and cell clusters are surrounded by desmoplastic stroma. When focal and without lymphovascular involvement, this is a low-risk pattern of invasion.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, pattern C
legend: Diffuse destructive invasion can take different forms. Most commonly, poorly formed glands at the invasive front will be seen, associated with desmoplastic stromal reaction and inflammation. With or without lymphovascular involvement, this is considered a high-risk pattern of invasion.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, pattern A
legend: This low-risk cervical tumour shows vaguely lobular to haphazard glands that are predominantly round and smooth. No stromal reaction or other destructive features are identified.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, with villoglandular architecture
legend: Elongated thin papillae are lined by usual pattern mucin-depleted tumour cells.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, mucinous not otherwise specified (NOS) pattern
legend: The tumour cells show evident pale mucinous cytoplasm reminiscent of normal endocervix.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, mucinous signet ring pattern
legend: Well-developed mucinous vacuoles push the tumour nuclei to the periphery of the cells. Background extracellular mucin is also seen.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, showing usual pattern cytological features (conventional Pap smear)
legend: A 3D cluster of malignant glandular cells are radially arranged and show a feathery appearance, resembling adenocarcinoma in situ; however, there is nuclear size and shape heterogeneity, and nucleoli are conspicuous.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV associated, with micropapillary architecture
legend: Tumours with this pattern often exhibit prominent lymphovascular space invasion.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV associated
legend: This particular tumour shows mucin-poor foci and other areas with intestinal differentiation including goblet cells.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV associated
legend: As expected, the tumour exhibits block-type p16 staining.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, with stratified mucin-producing pattern
legend: Irregular nests of mucin-rich cells with solid and stratified architecture and peripheral palisading of nuclei are characteristic.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated
legend: Usual and mucinous signet ring patterns are evident in this tumour.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, with microglandular architecture
legend: Smaller glands predominate in this example.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, with stratified mucin-producing pattern
legend: There is p63 positivity in the peripheral aspects of the tumour nests.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated
legend: Prominent mitoses and apoptotic bodies are seen.

title: Table 4.XXX Histological patterns of HPV-associated cervical adenocarcinoma
tablehtml:
Usual pattern

Mucinous pattern

This pattern accounts for ~75% of all cervical adenocarcinomas {29135516; 12207781}. Cells with abundant mucinous cytoplasm visible on morphology constitute 0–50% of the tumour, and the tumour otherwise shows mucin depletion.

This pattern accounts for ~10% of all cervical adenocarcinomas {29135516; 30679193}. There is intracytoplasmic mucin visible on morphology in the majority of the tumour, typically with a minor component of usual adenocarcinoma. Extracellular mucin may be seen. This pattern is subdivided into the following morphologies*:

Variable architectural arrangements including glandular, papillary, micropapillary, villoglandular, and solid morphologies are possible.

Mucinous NOS adenocarcinoma: mucinous cytoplasm resembling normal endocervix with pale purple staining on H&E

Intestinal adenocarcinoma: prominent goblet cell differentiation

Signet-ring cell adenocarcinoma: loose non-cohesive round cells with a mucinous vacuole displacing the nucleus

Stratified mucin-producing carcinoma: sometimes associated with adjacent stratified mucin-producing intraepithelial lesion and composed of invasive nests of stratified epithelium with intracytoplasmic mucin

*Although ≥ 50% of the tumour is classically required to show the mucinous morphology for designation as a specific mucinous pattern neoplasm, the presence of any of the mucinous appearances above, in any quantity, should be documented.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, with non-destructive growth along the endocervical surface (pattern A, low risk)
legend: The tumour carpets the endocervical surface with complex growth.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, with diffusely destructive invasion (pattern C, high risk)
legend: This relatively small cervical usual pattern tumour displays variably well formed glands. Diffuse desmoplastic reaction is evident. Adenocarcinoma in situ with more prominent mucinous differentiation is focally be seen along the surface.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, with papillary growth and focal destructive invasion (pattern B, low risk)
legend: This cervical tumour displays a prominent papillary exophytic and endophytic architecture. Focally, more poorly formed glands and clusters are seen, surrounded by reactive stroma.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, involving pelvic lymph node
legend: Large volume metastatic disease is seen (same case as previous slide with bulky papillary growth, diffusely destructive invasion and lymphovascular involvement).

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, involving lung
legend: This cervical primary shows easily identifiable apically located mitotic figures. There is mucinous differentiation including possible goblet cells.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, involving lung (p16 immunohistochemistry)
legend: The tumour shows strong overexpression of p16 in every cell.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, with bulky papillary growth, diffusely destructive invasion and lymphovascular involvement (pattern C, high risk)
legend: The tumour obliterates the endocervical surface. Confluent papillary growth is seen as are poorly formed glands at the invasive front. Adenocarcinoma in situ with a partial stratified mucin-producing morphology is focally seen along the surface.

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, in fragmented/superficial biopsy material
legend: The tumour shows evident complex architecture and prominent mucinous differentiation (not otherwise specified).

diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, HPV-associated, in fragmented/superficial biopsy material (HPV ISH)
legend: The tumour cells are positive for high risk mRNA HPV in situ hybridization; note the variety of signals (same case as previous slide with fragmented/superficial biopsy material).
